name: qr-scanner
purpose: Camera QR scanner — full-bleed video on the nimiq-blue gradient with a gold corner-frame viewport (pulsing while scanning), a white cancel pill and camera-failure guidance; scanning is powered by the qr-scanner library.

props.name: reportFrequency
props.description: Minimum ms between repeated 'result' emits for the same scan result.

props.name: validate
props.description: (scanResult: string) => boolean; results failing it are not emitted.

notes: Sample state: the inactive/idle shell in a 300x300 box — the ONLY state a headless or permission-less context can show. The camera cannot run headless, so the pixel contract covers: video at opacity 0 (never .ready) over the nq-blue radial gradient, the corner-frame overlay with .inactive (white 40% stroke instead of gold, pulse animation off), the 'Your device does not have an accessible camera.' warning, and the white Cancel pill. JS-MEASURED GEOMETRY: repositionOverlay() sizes the overlay to ceil(2/3 * min(w,h)) = 200px and centers it (top/left 50px), written into element.style — the html variant freezes those numbers inline; recompute for other host sizes. SPECIFICITY TRAP: the scoped .cancel-button rules (background white, nimiq-blue text) tie with nimiq-style's .nq-button-s.inverse at (0,2,0) and win only through the scope attribute + source order — the truth keeps [data-v-scanner] on them; the html variant gets the same result from .qr-scanner .cancel-button. LIVE SCANNING (Vue variant only): wires the qr-scanner npm dep (QrScannerLib on the video element) — it needs a real camera, a user gesture in most browsers, and a secure context (HTTPS or localhost; getUserMedia is unavailable on plain HTTP). Camera access failures flip to the inactive state with per-browser unblock instructions (Chrome/Firefox/Safari, mobile vs desktop — BrowserDetection from @nimiq/utils is inlined) and retry every 3s. Emits 'result' (throttled by reportFrequency + validate), 'cancel', 'error'. The html variant is the static shell only.
